title: Set a printer paper tray's guides snug to a fresh A4 stack
instruction: Set this tray's paper guides for the A4 paper so it feeds straight: the stack square against the feed edge and lying flat, every guide against it but not squeezing it. Then let go.
context: Refilling a printer's paper tray is something most people who print at home or in an office have done. A tray set for another size, or paper dropped in short of the feed edge, is a common cause of skewed prints and jams; a guide pushed hard against the stack bows it and jams just as often. The guides lock in place and slide only while their latch is squeezed.
setup: Station table; x forward from the line through the arm bases, y to the robot's left, table top 0 (mm). A laser printer's 250-sheet Tray 2 cassette lies on the table, pulled out, front panel and handle toward the robot's right: dark grey plastic, 304 x 417 mm outside, 3 mm floor, a 65 mm front panel (inside face, the feed edge, at y -160) and 30 mm side and back walls. Paper path centred on x 270. Two light grey width guides (36 mm tall, 100 mm long, y -70 to 30), linked so they move together, start at the widest setting, 218 mm apart (faces at x 161 and 379). A light grey length guide (140 mm wide) starts set for Legal, its face 356 mm from the feed edge (y 196). Each guide face is a 3 mm sprung pad (1,500 N/m) that presses in flush with the guide after 3 mm. The near width guide and the length guide each carry a blue squeeze latch: a 30 mm wide post and a 4 mm lever 6 mm from it, standing 26 mm above the guide; the guide slides only while the lever is squeezed toward the post (about 4 N), and stays where it is let go. In the tray: 100 sheets of A4 80 g/m2 copy paper as four 25-sheet bundles (210 x 297 x 2.5 mm, 125 g each). Lot A (screenshot): bundles, bottom to top, lie 3, 20, 37 and 54 mm short of the feed edge (staggered 17 mm apart), x offsets +0.8, -0.6, +0.5, -0.8 mm, turned +0.4, -0.5, +0.7, -0.3 degrees. Lot B: 54, 37, 20 and 3 mm short, offsets and turns reversed in sign. Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged; the screenshot shows lot A.
scoring: Per trial, scored at the end. 0 unless no gripper part is within 5 mm of the paper, the guides or their latches, both latches are let go, and the paper and guides have been still for 1 s. 0 if any guide's pad is pressed in more than 2 mm (3 N: the stack is squeezed and bows), or any bundle is tilted more than 2 degrees or lies higher than the stack. Otherwise: 0.5 when the length guide's face is within 1 mm of the stack's rear edge and every bundle is square (turned no more than 1 degree) with its leading edge within 1 mm of the feed edge; plus 0.5 when each width guide's face is within 1 mm of the stack's side. Trials are run on each of lots A and B and averaged.
reset_notes: 1. Squeeze each latch and slide the width guides to their widest stop (218 mm apart) and the length guide to the Legal mark (356 mm from the feed edge). 2. Fan a 100-sheet A4 pile into four 25-sheet bundles. 3. Lot A: lay them bottom to top 3, 20, 37 and 54 mm short of the feed edge, centred across the tray within 1 mm, each turned under 1 degree as listed. Lot B: 54, 37, 20 and 3 mm short. 4. Measure gaps with a 1 mm feeler gauge; read a pad's press from its scale.
fidelity: True-size cassette, guides and A4 stack. The stack is four sliding 25-sheet bundles, each rigid. Bowing is a stand-in rule: a guide pad pressed in more than 2 mm (3 N). The latch is a sprung lever; while it is shut a rule frees the guide, otherwise a stiff drive holds it. The far width guide follows the near one through a drive, as the rack does. Two lots vary the fan and skew, not the guide end positions, so a replay is not ruled out.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (mean of lots A and B; both arms rise and hover beside the tray, nothing is touched); demo: 1.0 in each lot
